name: Generate compliant food labels and nutrition panels
summary: Turns a product's recipe into a draft ingredient declaration, a per 100 g nutrition panel and the allergens it contains, written as a draft row in the business's own Airtable. Crons read and draft only; a person checks each draft against the Food Standards Code before any label is used.

recipe-to-label.evidence: 0 discovery calls for this workflow; 3 platform briefs read (epif, foodworks, mrpeasy), none mapped in the kit

covered_by.trigger-new-product: intake (new row in the Products table)
covered_by.nutrition-calc: draft (per 100 g panel from the Ingredients table)

crons.name: intake
crons.summary: New product rows from the Products table.

crons.name: draft
crons.summary: Work out each new product's declaration, per 100 g panel and allergens, and write one draft row per product.

draft_ops_note: Draft operations reach nobody outside the business: reads of the Products, Recipe and Ingredients tables, and a new row in the Drafts table. No operation sends, publishes or changes a record a customer sees.

airtable.covers: product list, recipe lines, ingredient nutrition, and draft rows in a Drafts table

gaps: Unleashed: its Bill of Materials and Products operations are mapped (docs.get_BillOfMaterials, docs.get_Products) but its HMAC signer is not built, so every call throws 'calls are not wired yet'. Recipes can come from Unleashed once the signer exists; that is a core runtime change and was not made here.
epif, FoodWorks and MRPeasy: not in core/sdk/platforms, so nothing can be called. FoodWorks help centre sections returned HTTP 403 and were not read.
Airtable list reads take one page (up to 100 rows) because the paging query parameters are not mapped in the kit.
Nutrition is per 100 g only: no per serving column, no percentage of daily intake, and no rounding rules from the Food Standards Code. The draft values are unrounded to one decimal place.
Sub-recipes (an ingredient that is itself a recipe) are not expanded; each recipe line must name an ingredient in the Ingredients table.
Allergens come from a list a person keeps on each ingredient. This is not a legal allergen declaration and does not handle may-contain statements.
Claims check, label artwork, proof approval, printing, and supplier specification updates are judgment or outside the kit: the agent skill covers the judgment; the rest has no mapped operation.
No live operation is mapped, so nothing is queued for approval. A label sent to a printer or a customer needs a live operation added once a platform for it is mapped.

evidence.platforms: 3 platform briefs (epif, foodworks, mrpeasy); none is mapped in the kit. Unleashed is mapped for recipes but not callable yet.
